data.name: Falguniya
data.gender_notes: Falguniya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Falguniya is a Sanskrit name derived from Falgun, the Hindu goddess of spring. The name represents the joy, warmth, and renewal that comes with the arrival of spring. Falguniya is also believed to symbolize the victory of good over evil, as the goddess is known to vanquish the demon of winter. The name Falguniya carries the meaning “Goddess of spring” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Falguniya usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of spring and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the beauty and rebirth of nature
data.etymology: Falguniya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of spring.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Falguniya total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Falguniya has roots in Hindu culture and is commonly found among communities that practice this ancient faith. The name is reminiscent of the changing seasons and the promise of new growth that comes with spring. In celebrations of Falgun, the Hindu month dedicated to this deity, devotees offer prayers and perform various rituals to seek her blessings for health, prosperity, and happiness.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Falguniya reflects the cyclical nature of life and the transformation that is inherent in existence. It is a constant reminder of the beauty and rebirth that can be found in the natural world, as well as the potential for renewal and spiritual growth within each individual. Additionally, the vanquishing of the demon of winter by the goddess Falgun signifies the triumph of light over darkness and the power of positivity and love to overcome adversity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Falguniya: Radiant and vibrant like the red hue of the month Falgun, symbolizing the inner warmth and joy that ignites the spirit during this season.

historical_references.reference: The Purana text 'Brahma Vaivarta Purana' mentions a Yaksha named Falguni, who is the lord of all seasons and the ruler of spring. He is also known as Falguniya.
In ancient Indian literature, the name 'Falguniya' is associated with the Hindu god of love, Kamadeva. Falguniya is often considered as his sister or wife, and is also known as the goddess of spring.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient to medieval (circa 2nd millennium BC to 16th century AD)
